title: Microsoft Teams: voice phishing detection for external calls
summary: Hold: the briefing treats a PowerShell parameter's default as confirmation that alerts will automatically reach users at release, which Microsoft has not stated. Its call-reporting advice also omits the documented licensing and reporting-setting prerequisites.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans voice phishing detection for one-to-one Teams calls with people outside the user's organisation.
claims.quote: Voice phishing detection helps protect Microsoft Teams users from potential scams during one-to-one calls with people outside their organization.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -VoicePhishingDetection None to select the no-alert mode, subject to the unreleased-feature caveat.
claims.quote:
Use this cmdlet to update values in existing Teams Calling Policies.
[-Identity] <string>
[-VoicePhishingDetection <String>]
None: No alerts.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope
claims.claim: New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy also has the VoicePhishingDetection parameter.
claims.quote:
### -VoicePhishingDetection

The Voice Phishing Detection policy enables AI-based detection of voice phishing (vishing) attempts during live inbound Microsoft Teams calls.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamscallingpolicy to sources for the statement that New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy has this parameter.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No Teams admin center setting or label for the voice phishing alert modes is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "VoicePhishingDetection" "Teams admin center"; opened Calling policies in Teams and Teams settings and policies reference, searched the latter for phishing/Scam, and read Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. No UI setting found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The feature is on by default and users should expect warnings automatically at release unless their calling policy says otherwise.
claims.quote: Searched: "voice phishing" "default" Teams; "VoicePhishingDetection" tenant switch group assignment default. Read Set-/New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy: BannerAndAudio is a parameter default, but the setting has no effect yet; automatic release activation is not stated.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Replace the first paragraph of Why it matters with: 'Microsoft lists BannerAndAudio as the parameter default, but says the setting currently has no effect. Microsoft has not stated whether alerts will automatically reach users when the feature is released.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no feature-specific entitlement has been published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Replace the licensing notes and first sentence of Cost and licensing with: 'Users need a Microsoft Teams license to use Teams. Microsoft has not published an additional licence requirement specific to voice phishing detection.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The feature is described as warning the recipient, rather than blocking or ending the call.
claims.quote: alerts recipients when suspicious activity is detected, helping them recognize potential threats and decide how to proceed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can report suspicious calls as a security concern without any stated entitlement or reporting-setting qualification.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious or suspicious calls in Microsoft Teams.
claims.fix: Qualify the reporting statement with: 'In organisations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, users can report suspicious calls when Report call is enabled in the Teams calling policy. Reporting must also be enabled in the Defender portal for reported calls to show up correctly.' Change the At rollout reminder to begin 'Where call reporting is enabled,'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The reporting documentation describes reporting a call marked Scam Suspected as not a security concern.
claims.quote:
In the Teams call history, locate the call that incorrectly flagged as "Scam Suspected".
Hover over the call without selecting it.
Select **...** > **Report as not a security concern**.

claims.quote: # End user reporting for Teams Calling (Preview)

claims.quote: Searched: "voice phishing" "Scam Suspected" Teams. Read End user reporting for Teams Calling and Set-/New-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; the reporting article does not identify voice phishing detection as the flag's source.
